audit_findings.title: Growth may require acquisition spending that owner earnings excludes
audit_findings.magnitude: 2023-2024 acquisitions used $2,212.776m versus $1,098.6m of owner earnings; changing modeled growth from 4%-7% to 0% reduces value by $29.30-$55.74 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Projected OE growth includes acquired earnings, while acquisition purchase prices and future acquisition financing are excluded from OE and the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Our recent historical growth has depended, and our future growth is likely to continue to depend, in part on our acquisition strategy and the successful integration of acquired businesses into our existing operations.
audit_findings.explanation: Historical reliance is demonstrated: organic sales declined 2.5% in both 2024 and 2025, while acquisitions/divestitures contributed 4.8% and 6.0%, respectively. Whether future 4%-7% growth can be organic is unresolved. The modeled growth spread changes value materially, although even the $175.83 bull value remains below the $318.36 market price.
audit_findings.action: Decompose historical OE growth into organic and acquired components; model acquisition purchase prices, incremental financing, and resulting share or interest costs, then rerun base and bull cases.

audit_findings.title: Net-investment hedge liability may be an unbridged claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $58.344m latest net derivative liability, equal to $1.03 per share and 0.6%-0.9% of scenario values
audit_findings.mechanism: Any net economic derivative liability not offset by the hedged foreign investments would require a bridge deduction from equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: Any increases or decreases related to the remeasurement of the effective portion of the hedges are recorded in the currency translation component of Accumulated other comprehensive income (loss) within Shareholders' Equity in the Consolidated Balance Sheets until the sale or substantial liquidation of the underlying investments.
audit_findings.explanation: The liability is filed and its omission from the bridge is demonstrated, but whether it is a separate economic claim is unresolved because the cross-currency swaps hedge foreign net investments and their effective remeasurement is offset through currency translation. Even deducting the entire latest net derivative liability would reduce value by only $1.03 per share, versus the $142.53 gap between market price and bull value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each latest-quarter cross-currency swap to the translated value of its hedged foreign net investment and deduct only any residual net economic liability.

audit_findings.title: Unfunded retiree obligations may not be fully captured by periodic expense
audit_findings.magnitude: $43.737m postretirement liability plus $41.538m pension liability, or $85.275m and $1.50 per share as a full-liability upper bound
audit_findings.mechanism: A deficit not represented by normalized benefit expense or cash payments would reduce the equity bridge; recurring benefit costs otherwise enter OE through earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: We sponsor an unfunded postretirement health care benefit plan covering certain of our United States employees.
audit_findings.explanation: The liabilities are demonstrated, but an OE or bridge error is not: periodic benefit costs are already included in earnings, and the pension liability cannot be evaluated without associated plan assets. Even deducting both latest balance-sheet liability lines in full would reduce value by only $1.50 per share, about 0.9%-1.3% of scenario values and immaterial to the market-price conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a latest-date funded-status schedule including plan assets, compare normalized cash contributions and benefit payments with expense embedded in OE, and bridge only a residual deficit not already captured.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may capitalize a nonrecurring tax benefit
audit_findings.magnitude: $4.363m computed FY2025 tax benefit from the filed 0.73% valuation-allowance rate item; approximately $0.91-$1.34 per share of DCF sensitivity
audit_findings.mechanism: An unremoved one-time tax benefit increases anchor OE and is then grown and capitalized through the forecast and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The effective tax rate decreased 130 basis points primarily due to a decline in federal valuation allowances.
audit_findings.explanation: The tax benefit is demonstrated, but whether the OE construction already normalized it is unresolved. The filed rate reconciliation implies a $4.363m benefit, only 0.77% of the $564.5m anchor. Removing it proportionally would reduce scenario values by approximately $0.91-$1.34 per share, insufficient to affect the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $4.363m valuation-allowance benefit through the anchor calculation and rerun all scenarios with a normalized tax rate if it remains included.

audit_findings.title: A completed divestiture creates a small anchor and perimeter normalization issue
audit_findings.magnitude: $12.545m charge, equal to 2.22% of anchor OE and a computed $2.62-$3.86 per-share DCF sensitivity; disposed-business earnings unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Retaining the noncash charge understates anchor OE, while retaining earnings from the disposed operations overstates continuing OE and its capitalized value.
audit_findings.evidence: Excluding the non-cash divestiture and related charges of $ 12,545 recorded in 2025, the operating results of the medical contract manufacturing business were not material to our Consolidated Financial Statements for any period presented.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether the charge and disposed-business results remain in the anchor is unresolved. Even if the entire $12.545m charge remained, its proportional valuation effect would be only $2.62-$3.86 per share and would not alter the conclusion relative to the $318.36 price. The disposed-business earnings are unquantified, but the filing states that its operating results were not material for any presented period.
audit_findings.action: Trace the charge through the OE reconciliation and remove it if included; separately exclude the sold and closing operations' earnings, working capital, and maintenance capital before finalizing the anchor.
